mainTopic: The king's share of spoils, the limit on a king's wives (eighteen and its source), and aggadot about דוד's family and the story of אמנון and תמר
overview: The amud opens by finishing the rule of the king's share of war spoils. Just as צדוק the כהן גדול takes half of the לחם הפנים and the other כהנים share the other half, the king takes half the spoils and his soldiers share the rest. A new משנה then teaches that a king may not marry too many wives. The תנא קמא sets the limit at eighteen. רבי יהודה allows more if they do not turn his heart away. רבי שמעון forbids even one wife who turns his heart, and limits the number even for righteous wives like אביגיל. The גמרא resolves an apparent contradiction with these תנאים' views on using the reason behind a verse (טעמא דקרא). It then derives eighteen from דוד's six wives in חברון and the נביא's words 'כהנה וכהנה', and notes ברייתות that count 24 or 48. Next it defends the count of six by showing that עגלה is מיכל, and it defines wives and concubines. The amud closes with aggadic teachings about דוד's children and the story of אמנון and תמר, ending with a decree whose content continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The king splits the spoils like the כהן גדול splits the bread
steps.stepSummary: A verse places the king next to צדוק the כהן גדול. So just as צדוק takes half and his brothers take half, the king takes half the spoils and his men take half.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And they anointed him to ה' as leader, and צדוק as כהן.' It compares the leader to צדוק. Just as צדוק gets half and his brothers get half, so too the leader gets half and his brothers get half.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a verse to prove that the king takes half of the war spoils for himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse mentions the king (נגיד) and צדוק together, and the גמרא reads this as a comparison (היקש). Whatever is true of צדוק's share applies to the king. צדוק takes half and the other כהנים share half, so the king takes half and the rest of the army shares half.

keyTerms.meaning: Compares (sets up a היקש, linking two things in one verse)
His brothers: the other כהנים, or for the king, the soldiers

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule for how a Jewish king divides war spoils with his army.

phrases.english: "And they anointed [him] to the Lord as leader, and Tzadok"
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 29:22. The leader here is שלמה המלך.

phrases.english: It compares the leader to Tzadok:
Just as Tzadok: half is for him
phrases.notes: This is half of the לחם הפנים, the bread the כהנים divide each week.

phrases.english: and half is for his brothers,
so too the leader: half is for him
and half is for his brothers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the earlier discussion of the king's share of spoils by giving the verse that proves it.
steps.raayaObject: The king takes half the spoils, and his men share the other half.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברי הימים א 29:22, which places the נגיד next to צדוק (a היקש).

steps.title: Where do we learn that צדוק takes half?
steps.stepSummary: The proof depends on צדוק taking half, so the גמרא asks for the source of that rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: And צדוק himself, how do we know he takes half?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule it just relied on: that the כהן גדול takes half. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A comparison only works if the thing you compare to is already proven. The גמרא wants to see where the Torah says the כהן גדול gets half of the לחם הפנים.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: And Tzadok himself, from where do we derive it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the base of the comparison in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source showing that the כהן גדול takes half of the לחם הפנים.

steps.title: רבי learns it from 'for אהרן and his sons'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי: the verse 'it shall be for אהרן and his sons' means half for אהרן and half for his sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי says, 'And it shall be for אהרן and for his sons': half for אהרן and half for his sons.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא: the verse about the לחם הפנים splits it between אהרן and his sons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse lists אהרן separately from his sons, as two parties. רבי reads this as an even split: one half to אהרן, the כהן גדול, and one half to all the other כהנים together.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught (in a ברייתא)

steps.whatToRemember: The king takes half the spoils, like the כהן גדול takes half the לחם הפנים. That rule comes from 'לאהרן ולבניו': half to אהרן, half to his sons.

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi says:
"And it shall be for Aaron and for his sons":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 24:9, about the לחם הפנים.

phrases.english: half for Aaron and half for his sons.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ויקרא 24:9 'לאהרן ולבניו' means half to אהרן and half to his sons.

steps.title: New משנה: a king may marry no more than eighteen wives
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה opens: the Torah says a king may not have many wives, and the limit is eighteen.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: 'He shall not have many wives': only eighteen.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. The first opinion (תנא קמא) says the king's limit is eighteen wives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah only says 'not many' and gives no number. The תנא קמא sets an exact number: eighteen is allowed, more is forbidden. This reading counts wives by number, without asking what kind of wives they are.

keyTerms.meaning: He (the king) shall not have many wives

phrases.english: MISHNA: "He shall not have many wives",
phrases.notes: דברים 17:17

phrases.english: but only eighteen.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא יַרְבֶּה לוֹ נָשִׁים, אֶלָּא שְׁמֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A king may marry up to eighteen wives and no more.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: more is allowed if they don't turn his heart
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the king may marry many wives, as long as they do not lead his heart away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: He may marry many, as long as they do not turn his heart away.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the eighteen limit and says the number depends on whether the wives lead him astray.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse goes on to say 'and his heart shall not turn away'. רבי יהודה treats that as the reason for the ban. So if the wives will not turn his heart, the reason does not apply, and many wives are allowed.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: מַרְבֶּה הוּא לוֹ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: He may take many for himself,

phrases.aramaic: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יְהוּ מְסִירוֹת אֶת לִבּוֹ.
phrases.english: provided that they do not turn his heart away.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: מַרְבֶּה הוּא לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא's fixed number.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Many wives are allowed if they do not turn the king's heart away.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: not even one wife who turns his heart
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says even a single wife is forbidden to the king if she would turn his heart away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: Even one wife, if she turns his heart away, he may not marry her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון gives a third opinion: a wife who leads the king astray is forbidden even if she is his only wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון, 'his heart shall not turn away' is its own separate ban, not linked to the number of wives. So one bad influence is already forbidden. This leaves him with the question of what 'not many wives' adds, which the next step asks.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: Even one,
if she turns his heart away,
he may not marry her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third opinion, stricter than רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even one wife is forbidden to the king if she turns his heart away.

steps.title: Then why does the verse say 'not many wives'?
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון asks himself: if a bad wife is forbidden anyway, what does 'not many wives' teach?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does it say 'He shall not have many wives'?
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the משנה, רבי שמעון asks what the words 'not many wives' add to his view. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the problem were only wives who turn his heart, the verse could have banned just those. Saying 'not many' must teach something more, beyond the bad-influence ban.

phrases.english: If so, why is it stated:
"He shall not have many wives"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי שמעון asks about his own reading of the verse.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What extra rule the words 'not many wives' teach in רבי שמעון's view.

steps.title: Even wives as righteous as אביגיל
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון answers: the number limit applies even to righteous wives like אביגיל.
steps.simpleTranslation: To teach that even if they are like אביגיל, he still may not marry many.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון explains that 'not many wives' forbids too many wives even when every one of them is righteous, like אביגיל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון ends up with two separate bans. One forbids any wife who turns his heart. The other forbids too many wives, even good ones like אביגיל, who actually kept דוד from sinning. Unlike רבי יהודה, he does not let the verse's reason cancel the number limit.

keyTerms.meaning: אביגיל, the wise and righteous wife of דוד

steps.whatToRemember: Three views: the תנא קמא allows eighteen. רבי יהודה allows more if they don't turn his heart. רבי שמעון forbids even one who turns his heart, and also limits the number even for righteous wives like אביגיל.

phrases.english: That even [if they are] like Abigail.
phrases.notes: אביגיל stopped דוד from killing נבל (שמואל א פרק 25), so even wives that good still count toward the limit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי שמעון's question in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Not many wives' forbids too many wives even if they are all righteous like אביגיל.

steps.title: Don't these two תנאים usually hold the opposite?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that here רבי יהודה uses the verse's reason and רבי שמעון does not. But elsewhere we hear the reverse.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Does this mean that רבי יהודה uses the reason behind a verse, and רבי שמעון does not use the reason behind a verse? But we have heard them hold the opposite!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that this משנה seems to switch רבי יהודה's and רבי שמעון's usual positions, and challenges it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה, רבי יהודה allows many wives once the reason (turning his heart) does not apply, so he uses the reason to set the law. רבי שמעון keeps the number limit even for good wives, so he does not. But elsewhere we know רבי שמעון is the one who uses the reason behind a verse (דרשינן טעמא דקרא) and רבי יהודה does not, so the views look reversed.

keyTerms.meaning: Uses the reason behind a verse to decide the law

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up who holds what! In this משנה רבי יהודה is the one using the reason. Usually it is רבי שמעון who is known for דרשינן טעמא דקרא, and that is exactly why the גמרא is surprised.
steps.whyThisMatters: Whether we use a verse's reason to set the law is a basic disagreement across ש״ס, so the גמרא wants each תנא to stay consistent.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Is this to say that Rabbi Yehuda
interprets the reason of the verse,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לָא דָּרֵישׁ טַעְמָא דִּקְרָא?
phrases.english: and Rabbi Shimon does not interpret the reason of the verse?
But we have heard them [hold] the opposite!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה דָּרֵישׁ טַעְמָא דִּקְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the opinions of the משנה and finds a contradiction with their views elsewhere.
steps.kashyaTarget: The positions of רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון in the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Elsewhere רבי שמעון uses the reason behind a verse and רבי יהודה does not. Here it looks reversed, so each seems to contradict himself.

steps.title: The widow's pledge: the opposite pattern
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows רבי יהודה forbidding a pledge from any widow based on the plain words, while רבי שמעון limits it to a poor widow based on the reason behind the law.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: you may not take a pledge from a widow, whether she is poor or rich, because the פסוק says 'Do not take a widow's garment as a pledge.' This is רבי יהודה's view. רבי שמעון says: from a rich widow you may take a pledge; from a poor widow you may not, because you must give it back to her, and you would give her a bad name among her neighbors.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is bringing the source for the contradiction it raised in step 9. This ברייתא is where we see the 'reverse' positions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה reads the פסוק literally, so every widow is protected. רבי שמעון limits the law to a poor widow, since the problem only exists when the pledge has to be returned. That looks like he is reasoning from why the Torah gave the law.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
Taking a pledge (collateral) for a loan
Do not take as a pledge
A bad name, a bad reputation

phrases.english: As it is taught: a widow,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין שֶׁהִיא עֲנִיָּה בֵּין שֶׁהִיא עֲשִׁירָה,
phrases.english: whether she is poor or whether she is rich,
we do not take a pledge from her,
as it says: 'Do not take a widow's garment as a pledge.'
phrases.notes: דברים 24:17

phrases.english: These are the words of רבי יהודה.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: עֲשִׁירָה – מְמַשְׁכְּנִין אוֹתָהּ,
phrases.english: רבי שמעון says: a rich widow, we may take a pledge from her;
a poor widow, we may not take a pledge from her,
and you are obligated to return it to her,
and you give her a bad name among her neighbors.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the 'elsewhere we hear the reverse' claim of step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That elsewhere רבי שמעון uses the reason of a פסוק and רבי יהודה does not.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about taking a pledge from a widow.

steps.title: Explaining רבי שמעון's words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא clarifies that רבי שמעון's two clauses are one chain: taking the pledge forces you to keep returning it, and that ruins her reputation.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we asked: what is רבי שמעון saying? This is what he means: since you take a pledge from her, you must return it to her, and so you give her a bad name among her neighbors.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון's words sound like two separate points, so the גמרא explains how they connect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a poor person, the Torah requires returning the pledge when it is needed, so the lender keeps coming to her house. Neighbors who see this may suspect something improper. That is the reason he gives for the law, and it only applies to a poor widow.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, because of the fact that

phrases.english: And we said: what is he saying?
This is what he is saying:
since you take a pledge from her,
you are obligated to return it to her,
phrases.notes: This is the rule of giving back a poor person's pledge when he needs it (דברים 24:12-13).

phrases.english: and so you give her a bad name among her neighbors.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies רבי שמעון's reasoning in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How רבי שמעון's two clauses fit together.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Taking the pledge forces repeated returns, which leads to a bad reputation.

steps.title: So who uses the Torah's reason?
steps.stepSummary: From the widow case the גמרא concludes that רבי יהודה does not use טעמא דקרא and רבי שמעון does, the reverse of the king's wives case.
steps.simpleTranslation: So we see that רבי יהודה does not interpret the reason of a פסוק, and רבי שמעון does interpret the reason of a פסוק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion from the widow case. This finishes laying out the contradiction, and the next steps will answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the king's wives, רבי יהודה used the reason ('as long as his heart is not turned') and רבי שמעון did not. Here it is the other way around, so each תנא seems to contradict himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Interprets the law based on the reason behind the פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: This is about the general rule of each תנא, not about widows or kings. The question is whether the reason behind a law can change who the law applies to.

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא דָּרֵישׁ טַעְמָא דִּקְרָא,
phrases.english: Evidently, רבי יהודה does not interpret the reason of the verse,
and רבי שמעון does interpret the reason of the verse.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא דָּרֵישׁ טַעְמָא דִּקְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference that completes the contradiction raised in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: Each Tanna's general approach to טעמא דקרא.

steps.title: Defending רבי יהודה: here the Torah states the reason
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה normally does not use reasons, but with the king the פסוק itself spells out the reason, so he follows it.
steps.simpleTranslation: In general, רבי יהודה does not interpret the reason of a פסוק. But here is different, because the פסוק explains its own reason: why 'he shall not have many wives'? Because 'his heart should not turn away.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction for רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה does not guess at reasons the Torah did not give. With the king, the Torah wrote the reason in the same פסוק, so using it is not guessing, and he can say many wives are allowed if they will not turn his heart.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that refusing to use reasons means not inventing them. When the Torah states the reason, even רבי יהודה uses it.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָלְמָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא דָּרֵישׁ טַעְמָא דִּקְרָא,
phrases.english: In general, רבי יהודה does not interpret the reason of the verse,
but here it is different,
because the verse spells out its reason:
What is the reason for 'he shall not have many wives'?
phrases.notes: דברים 17:17

phrases.english: Because 'his heart should not turn away.'

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָלְמָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא דָּרֵישׁ טַעְמָא דִּקְרָא, וְשָׁאנֵי הָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction for רבי יהודה's side.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: a stated reason versus an unstated one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה contradicts himself by using a reason with the king.
steps.terutzMaskana: He only refuses unstated reasons; with the king the reason is written in the פסוק.

steps.title: Defending רבי שמעון: the stated reason must teach something extra
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי שמעון would have figured out the reason himself, the written words 'לא יסור' must teach a new law: even one wife who turns his heart is forbidden. 'לא ירבה' then limits the number even of righteous wives like אביגיל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון would tell you: since in general we interpret the reason of a פסוק, the Torah could have written only 'he shall not have many wives' and stopped. I would have said on my own: why not many? So that his heart will not turn away. So why do I need 'his heart should not turn away'? To teach that even one wife who turns his heart away, he may not marry. Then how do I apply 'he shall not have many'? Even if they are like אביגיל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction for רבי שמעון, showing why here he does not use the reason to limit the law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון a written reason is extra, because he would have worked it out anyway. So 'לא יסור לבבו' becomes its own law, forbidding even one bad wife. Then 'לא ירבה' cannot just be about bad wives, so it limits the number even of good wives.

keyTerms.meaning: He would tell you, he can answer you
And let it be silent, stop there
How do I apply (this part of the פסוק)?
A righteous wife of דוד המלך

steps.whatToRemember: Both תנאים stay consistent. רבי יהודה ignores reasons the תורה does not state, but follows a stated one. רבי שמעון works out reasons himself, so a stated reason is extra and teaches a new law. That is why for him the king may not have many wives, even righteous ones like אביגיל.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון is not ignoring the reason here. He is so sure of it that he treats the written reason as extra words, which must teach a separate law.

phrases.english: And רבי שמעון would say to you:
Since in general we interpret the reason of the verse,

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן לִכְתּוֹב קְרָא ״לֹא יַרְבֶּה לוֹ נָשִׁים״
phrases.english: then let the verse write 'he shall not have many wives'
and stop there,
and I would say: what is the reason for 'he shall not have many'?
Because 'it should not turn away.'
So why do I need 'it should not turn away'?
Even one wife, if she turns his heart away,
he may not marry her.
Then how do I apply 'he shall not have many'?
That it applies even to wives like אביגיל.
phrases.notes: He means wives as righteous as אביגיל, who would never turn his heart. Even so, he may not have too many.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אָמַר לָךְ: מִכְּדִי בְּעָלְמָא דָּרְשִׁינַן טַעְמָא דִּקְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction for רבי שמעון's side, completing the defense of both תנאים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra words in the פסוק are used to teach a new law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון contradicts himself by not using the reason with the king.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because he uses reasons, the written reason is extra and teaches a new law (even one bad wife is forbidden). So 'לא ירבה' limits the number even of righteous wives.

steps.title: Where does the number eighteen come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's limit of eighteen wives for a king.
steps.simpleTranslation: These eighteen wives: where do we learn them from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new section by asking for the source of the number eighteen. This line sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 9-14 were about why a king is limited. Now the גמרא asks a different question: how do we know the exact number? The תורה only says 'לא ירבה' (he shall not have many) and gives no number.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know it? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: These eighteen, from where do we know them?
phrases.notes: He means the eighteen wives the משנה lets a king marry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the reason behind the limit to the source of the number.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for the number eighteen.

steps.title: Six wives in חברון, plus six and six more
steps.stepSummary: דוד had six wives in חברון, and the נביא said he could add 'like these and like those', meaning six more and six more, which makes eighteen.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק lists six sons born to דוד in חברון from six different wives. Then the נביא told him, 'If that is too little, I would add to you like these and like those.' 'Like these' means six more, and 'like those' means another six, which makes eighteen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers using two פסוקים. One counts דוד's six wives, and the other has the נביא offering him more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק sets the base number at six. The words 'כהנה וכהנה' are read as two more groups, each the same size as the first group. Six plus six plus six gives the משנה's eighteen.

phrases.english: As it is written: "And sons were born to David in Hebron
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 3:2-5

phrases.english: and his firstborn was Amnon, from Ahinoam the Jezreelitess;
and his second, Chileab, from Abigail
the wife of Nabal the Carmelite;
and the third, Absalom, son of Maacah ...
and the fourth, Adonijah, son of Haggith;
and the fifth, Shephatiah, son of Abital;
and the sixth, Ithream, from Eglah, David's wife.
These were born to David in Hebron."
phrases.notes: Six sons from six mothers, so that is six wives.

phrases.english: And the prophet said to him:
"If that were too little, I would add to you like these and like those."
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 12:8

phrases.english: "Like these" means six; "and like those" means six,
so that all together they are eighteen.
phrases.notes: The six he already had, plus six, plus six.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Six wives in חברון, plus 'כהנה' (6) and 'וכהנה' (6), which equals 18.

steps.title: רבינא: maybe the words double the total each time
steps.stepSummary: רבינא objects that 'כהנה וכהנה' could mean doubling: first up to 12, and then up to 24.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא challenges this: Say instead that 'like these' brings the total to twelve, and 'and like those' brings it to twenty-four.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא attacks the reading in step 16 by offering a different way to count the same words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 had each word add a fixed six. רבינא says each word could add an amount equal to everything counted so far. Six becomes twelve, and twelve becomes twenty-four, so the proof for eighteen is not certain.

phrases.english: Ravina objects to it:
Say instead: "like these" makes twelve,
"and like those" makes twenty-four.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how step 16 counted the words.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'כהנה' and 'וכהנה' each add six.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The words could just as well mean doubling the running total, which gives 24 and not 18.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports twenty-four
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that 'לא ירבה לו נשים' means no more than twenty-four, which matches רבינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא: 'He shall not have many wives' means more than twenty-four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that agrees with רבינא's count of twenty-four.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא's reading is more than his own idea, because a תנא held it too. So there is a real opinion that a king may marry up to twenty-four wives, against the משנה's eighteen.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a ברייתא supports it)
He shall not have many wives

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
"He shall not have many wives" means
phrases.notes: דברים 17:17

phrases.english: more than twenty-four.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבינא's reading.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on 'לא ירבה לו נשים'.

steps.title: Learning from the letter ו gives forty-eight
steps.stepSummary: Someone who learns extra meaning from the ו in 'וכהנה' doubles the total again, reaching forty-eight.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who learns something from the letter ו, it comes to forty-eight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a third way of counting, based on the extra letter ו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ו ('and') in 'וכהנה' is read as adding one more round of doubling. On top of רבינא's twenty-four, that gives forty-eight.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who learns something from

steps.confusionAlert: Three numbers come from the very same words: 18 (adding six each time), 24 (doubling), and 48 (doubling plus the extra ו). They are different ways of reading one פסוק.

phrases.english: According to the one who learns something from the letter vav,
phrases.notes: He means the ו at the start of 'וכהנה'.

phrases.english: they come to forty-eight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבינא's doubling and adds the ו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the ו is used to learn something, the limit is forty-eight wives.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports forty-eight
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא teaches that 'לא ירבה לו נשים' means no more than forty-eight.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: 'He shall not have many wives' means more than forty-eight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes by showing that the forty-eight reading also has a ברייתא behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each reading of 'כהנה וכהנה' has a source. The משנה says 18, one ברייתא says 24, and another ברייתא says 48.
steps.whatToRemember: The limit on a king's wives is learned from דוד's six wives and the נביא's words 'כהנה וכהנה'. Depending on how you count, the limit is 18 (the משנה), 24 (רבינא and a ברייתא), or 48 (learning from the ו, with a ברייתא).

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
"He shall not have many wives" means
more than forty-eight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the forty-eight reading.
steps.raayaObject: The count of forty-eight learned from the ו.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on 'לא ירבה לו נשים'.

steps.title: What is our משנה's reason for eighteen?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the תנא of our משנה limits the king to eighteen wives, when the ברייתות said twenty-four or forty-eight.
steps.simpleTranslation: And our תנא, what is his reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns back to our משנה, which said eighteen, and asks for its source. This sets up the next step, where רב כהנא will answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 17-20 showed that 'כהנה וכהנה' could be read as doubling, which gives 24 or 48. So the גמרא now needs to explain how our משנה reads the same words and gets only eighteen.

keyTerms.meaning: Our תנא, meaning the author of our משנה

phrases.english: And our tanna — what is his reason?
phrases.notes: He means the author of our משנה, who said a king may have eighteen wives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having shown the readings that give 24 and 48, the גמרא goes back to defend the משנה's eighteen.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the משנה reads 'כהנה וכהנה' so that it gives eighteen and not a doubling.

steps.title: The second 'like these' equals the first: six
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא explains that the second 'כהנה' is compared to the first, so each one adds exactly six.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: The verse compares the second 'כהנה' to the first. Just as the first means six, the second also means six.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא gives the משנה's reasoning. Both 'כהנה' words have the same value, so each adds six wives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא read the second 'כהנה' as doubling whatever total came before it. רב כהנא says no: the second 'כהנה' copies the first, which is a fixed six. So the count is 6 + 6 + 6 = 18.

keyTerms.meaning: Compares, treating one thing like another

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
It compares the latter 'like those' to the former 'like these':
just as the former 'like these' is six,
so too the latter 'like those' is six.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: מַקִּישׁ ״כָּהֵנָּה״ בָּתְרָא לְ״כָּהֵנָּה״ קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second 'כהנה' has the same value as the first, which is six, so the total is eighteen.

steps.title: But מיכל was also his wife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that דוד also had מיכל, so he had at least seven wives, not six.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there was מיכל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the starting number of six. מיכל was also דוד's wife, so it seems he had seven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole count of eighteen depends on the first 'כהנה' meaning exactly six. If מיכל was an extra wife, the starting number is wrong and so is the total.

keyTerms.meaning: מיכל, daughter of שאול and wife of דוד

phrases.english: But there was Michal!
phrases.notes: מיכל is not among the six wives listed in חברון, in שמואל ב 3:2-5.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the base number of six that steps 16 and 22 rely on.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that דוד had exactly six wives in חברון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מיכל was also his wife, so the count should be seven.

steps.title: עגלה is really מיכל
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that עגלה, one of the six wives, is מיכל. She was called עגלה because she was as dear to him as a calf, a term also found in שמשון's words.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: עגלה is מיכל. Why was she called עגלה? Because she was dear to him like a calf. And so the verse says: 'If you had not plowed with my calf...'
steps.whatsHappening: רב says מיכל is not an extra wife. She is already on the list under a nickname, עגלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If עגלה and מיכל are the same woman, the count stays at six. רב brings a פסוק where שמשון calls his wife 'my calf' to show that 'calf' is used as a loving name for a wife.

keyTerms.meaning: עגלה, one of דוד's wives in חברון; also means a calf
And so the verse says, used to bring a supporting פסוק

phrases.english: Rav said:
Eglah is Michal,
and why was she called Eglah?
Because she was dear to him like a calf.
And so it says:
'Had you not plowed with my calf, etc.'
phrases.notes: שופטים 14:18. שמשון calls his wife 'my calf.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identification: two names refer to one person.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מיכל was a seventh wife in addition to the six listed.
steps.terutzMaskana: מיכל is עגלה, so the list of six already includes her.

steps.title: But מיכל never had children
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that עגלה had a son, while a פסוק says מיכל had no child until the day she died.
steps.simpleTranslation: And did מיכל have children? But it is written: 'And מיכל the daughter of שאול had no child until the day of her death'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's claim that עגלה is מיכל. עגלה had a son, but the פסוק says מיכל had no child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the list of wives in חברון, each wife appears with her son, and עגלה is listed as the mother of יתרעם. If she is מיכל, that contradicts the פסוק saying מיכל was childless.

keyTerms.meaning: And were there? This is a doubting question

phrases.english: And did Michal have children?
phrases.notes: עגלה is listed with a son, יתרעם (שמואל ב 3:5), so if she is מיכל, then מיכל had a child.

phrases.english: But isn't it written:
'And Michal the daughter of Saul had no
child until the day of her death'!
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 6:23

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's answer from step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that עגלה is מיכל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: עגלה had a son, but the פסוק says מיכל had no child, so they cannot be the same woman.

steps.title: She had a child on the day she died
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא reads the פסוק carefully: before the day of her death she had no child, but on that day she did.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Until the day of her death she had no child. On the day of her death she had one.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא keeps רב's identification by reading the word 'until' strictly. The child was born on the very day מיכל died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only rules out children before the day of her death. So עגלה-מיכל could still be the mother of the son listed in חברון.

keyTerms.meaning: Until the day of her death
On the day of her death

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:

phrases.aramaic: עַד יוֹם מוֹתָהּ לֹא הָיָה לָהּ,
phrases.english: Until the day of her death she did not have one;
on the day of her death she had one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: עַד יוֹם מוֹתָהּ לֹא הָיָה לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the word 'until' in the פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק means מיכל never had any child at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: She had no child before her final day, but she did have one on that day.

steps.title: The children were born in חברון, but the incident was later in ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the children were born in חברון, while the פסוק about מיכל comes after an incident in ירושלים, when she was already punished. So רב חסדא's timing does not fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, where are the children counted? In חברון. But the incident with מיכל happened in ירושלים, as it is written: 'And מיכל the daughter of שאול looked out the window and saw King דוד leaping and dancing before ה', and she despised him.' And רב יהודה, or some say רב יוסף, said: מיכל received her punishment!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא. The son of עגלה was born early, in חברון. The 'no child' פסוק belongs to a later incident in ירושלים, and מיכל was punished right then.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא put מיכל's child at the very end of her life, but the child listed under עגלה was born years earlier in חברון. Also, the 'no child' פסוק describes a punishment that began at the ירושלים incident. So the פסוק is about the time after that incident, not about her last day.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, consider. This introduces a point everyone already knows
חברון, where דוד first ruled and his first sons were born
And some say. The same saying is told in another person's name

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּדֵי, בָּנִים הֵיכָא קָא חָשֵׁיב לְהוּ? בְּחֶבְרוֹן.
phrases.english: Now, where does it count the children? In Hebron.
Whereas the incident of Michal
was in Jerusalem, as it is written:
'And Michal the daughter of Saul looked out through the window
and saw King David
leaping and dancing before God, and she despised him.'
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 6:16

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב יוֹסֵף:
phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said, and some say Rav Yosef:
Michal received her punishment!
phrases.notes: Her punishment of having no children started right at that incident, so the 'no child' פסוק is about the time after it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדֵי, בָּנִים הֵיכָא קָא חָשֵׁיב לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב חסדא's answer in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's reading that מיכל's child was born on the day of her death.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The child listed under עגלה was born in חברון, early in דוד's reign. The childlessness was a punishment that began at the later incident in ירושלים. So a child born on her death day cannot be the חברון son.

steps.title: Before the incident she had a child, after it none
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the פסוק: מיכל had a child before the ירושלים incident, which is the חברון son, and none afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: until that incident she had a child; from then on she did not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops רב חסדא's reading and gives a new one. The 'no child' פסוק describes only the years after the ירושלים incident.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The son born in חברון came before the incident, so מיכל can be עגלה. The punishment of childlessness began only after she despised דוד. This saves רב's identification and the count of six wives, and so the משנה's eighteen.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say. This replaces an earlier explanation with a new one
From here on, from that point forward

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's eighteen depends on דוד having exactly six wives in חברון. מיכל is counted as עגלה. She had her son in חברון, and the 'no child' פסוק covers only the time after she despised דוד in ירושלים.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
until that incident, she had a child;
from then on, she did not have one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא: עַד אוֹתוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה – הָיָה לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב חסדא's answer after step 27 knocked it down.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reading of the פסוק's time frame.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'no child' פסוק covers her whole life up to her last day.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק covers only the time after the ירושלים incident. Her son from חברון came before it, so עגלה is מיכל and the count stays at six.

steps.title: A verse says דוד took more wives in ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the limited count of דוד's wives from a פסוק saying he took more wives and concubines in ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it written: 'And דוד took more concubines and wives in ירושלים'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a פסוק that seems to say דוד kept adding wives in ירושלים, beyond the count it has been working with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the גמרא has been working with a fixed number of wives, with eighteen as the most a king may take. This פסוק says דוד took 'more' wives and concubines after coming to ירושלים. That sounds like he went past the count, so the גמרא raises it as a challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written? This introduces a פסוק used to challenge what was just said.

phrases.english: But isn't it written: "And David took more
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 5:13

phrases.english: concubines and wives in Jerusalem"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the issue of עגלה and מיכל, the גמרא challenges the overall count of דוד's wives.
steps.kashyaTarget: The limited count of דוד's wives (eighteen at most)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'more' in the פסוק suggests דוד added wives beyond the limited number.

steps.title: The extra wives only completed eighteen
steps.stepSummary: The added wives in ירושלים only brought the total up to eighteen and no more.
steps.simpleTranslation: They were to fill up the eighteen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the wives taken in ירושלים did not go past the limit. They only filled up the total to eighteen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The six wives from חברון were not the full eighteen. So 'more' in the פסוק means he added wives until he reached eighteen. The limit stays in place.

phrases.english: To complete the eighteen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the פסוק in step 29.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'More' wives means דוד went past the limit.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'More' only means he added wives until he reached eighteen.

steps.title: What is the difference between wives and concubines
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the פסוק means by 'wives' and by 'concubines'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are 'wives' and what are 'concubines'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the פסוק it just quoted. It sets up the next step, which will define the two terms.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lists two kinds of women, נשים and פלגשים. The גמרא wants to know what legally separates them. This is a question to understand the terms, not an attack.

keyTerms.meaning: What is? A request for explanation

phrases.english: What are "wives" and what are "concubines"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the two terms from the פסוק quoted in step 29.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The legal difference between נשים and פלגשים

steps.title: Wives have כתובה and קידושין, concubines do not
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב: wives are married with כתובה and קידושין, while concubines have neither.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Wives come with a כתובה and קידושין. Concubines come without a כתובה and without קידושין.
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains that the difference is about formal marriage. A wife has קידושין and a כתובה, and a concubine has neither.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both kinds of women live with the man. A wife is bound to him through קידושין and protected by a כתובה, a marriage contract. A concubine lives with him without these legal steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Marriage contract that protects the wife
Betrothal, the act that legally makes a woman a man's wife

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda says that Rav says:
Wives are with a marriage contract and betrothal,
concubines are without a marriage contract and without betrothal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: נָשִׁים בִּכְתוּבָּה וּבְקִידּוּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: נשים have כתובה and קידושין; פלגשים have neither.
steps.whatToRemember: A wife has כתובה and קידושין. A פילגש has neither.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic definition of פילגש that later discussions build on.

steps.title: דוד's four hundred children of יפת תואר mothers
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב: דוד had four hundred children, all born to יפת תואר mothers. They were powerful leaders and the strongmen of דוד's kingdom.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: דוד had four hundred children. All of them were sons of יפת תואר women. They grew their hair in a gentile style, rode in golden carriages, walked at the head of the troops, and were the strongmen of the house of דוד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching of רב about דוד's family. It describes four hundred children of captive women and their role in the kingdom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their mothers were women captured in war, called יפת תואר. They wore a gentile hairstyle, rode in golden carriages, led the army, and backed up דוד's rule with force.

keyTerms.meaning: A beautiful woman captured in war whom a soldier may marry under special rules
A gentile hairstyle, a long lock of hair

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda says that Rav says:

phrases.aramaic: אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת יְלָדִים הָיוּ לוֹ לְדָוִד,
phrases.english: David had four hundred children,
and all of them were sons of beautiful captive women,
and they grew gentile-style locks of hair,
and all of them sat in carriages of gold,
and they walked at the head of the troops,

phrases.aramaic: וְהֵם הָיוּ בַּעֲלֵי אֶגְרוֹפִין שֶׁל בֵּית דָּוִד.
phrases.english: and they were the strongmen of the house of David.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת יְלָדִים הָיוּ לוֹ לְדָוִד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching about דוד's family, moving from his wives to his children.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד had four hundred sons from יפת תואר women, and they were the military backbone of his kingdom.

steps.title: תמר was the daughter of a יפת תואר
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב: תמר was the daughter of a יפת תואר. He cites תמר's words to אמנון as the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה also said in the name of רב: תמר was the daughter of a יפת תואר, as it says: 'Now, please speak to the king, for he will not keep me from you.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב makes a claim about תמר's mother and quotes a פסוק as his source. The next step explains how the פסוק proves it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תמר said this to אמנון, her half-brother, when he tried to force himself on her. She suggests that דוד would let אמנון marry her. רב uses these words to show something unusual about her lineage.

keyTerms.meaning: Daughter of דוד, half-sister of אמנון
As it is said, introducing a פסוק as a source

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda says that Rav says:
Tamar was the daughter of a beautiful captive woman,
as it is stated: "Now, therefore, please speak to the king,
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 13:13. תמר is speaking to אמנון.

phrases.english: for he will not withhold me from you."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: תָּמָר בַּת יְפַת תּוֹאַר הָיְתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching of רב יהודה in the name of רב about דוד's children, connected to the theme of יפת תואר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תמר's mother was a יפת תואר.

steps.title: Why the verse proves תמר's lineage
steps.stepSummary: If תמר were the daughter of a properly married wife, she would be אמנון's sister and forbidden to him. Since she said דוד would allow it, she must have been a יפת תואר's daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think she was the daughter of a married wife, would his sister be permitted to him? So learn from this that she was the daughter of a יפת תואר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the פסוק proves רב's claim. It shows that the other possibility makes no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man may never marry his sister. If תמר counted as אמנון's sister, דוד could never have allowed the marriage. Since תמר said he would, she must not have counted as his sister by law, which fits being a יפת תואר's daughter.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you think, introducing a possibility in order to reject it
Daughter of a properly married wife
Learn from it, a conclusion drawn from a proof

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think תמר was not דוד's child at all. The point is only that by law she did not count as אמנון's sister, so a marriage between them was possible.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ בַּת נִישּׂוּאִין הֲוַאי,
phrases.english: And if it enters your mind that she was the daughter of a married wife,
would his sister be permitted to him?
phrases.notes: 'His sister' means אמנון's sister, and 'him' is אמנון.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from it:
she was the daughter of a beautiful captive woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ בַּת נִישּׂוּאִין הֲוַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק in step 34 proves רב's claim.
steps.raayaObject: רב's claim that תמר was the daughter of a יפת תואר
steps.raayaSupportSource: תמר's words in שמואל ב 13:13 that דוד would not keep her from אמנון
steps.whatToRemember: תמר could have married אמנון because by law she did not count as his sister. Her mother was a יפת תואר.

steps.title: יונדב was wise for evil
steps.stepSummary: On the פסוק calling יונדב a wise man, רב יהודה in the name of רב says he was wise for wickedness.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And אמנון had a friend named יונדב, son of שמעה, דוד's brother, and יונדב was a very wise man.' רב יהודה said in the name of רב: wise for wickedness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a פסוק from the story of אמנון and תמר. רב explains that יונדב's 'wisdom' was cleverness used for evil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling יונדב 'wise' sounds like praise. But he used his cleverness to help אמנון plan his sin against תמר. So רב reads 'wise' here as clever in doing evil.

keyTerms.meaning: And so on, meaning the פסוק continues

phrases.english: "And Amnon had a friend whose name was Jonadab,
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 13:3

phrases.english: son of Shimeah, David's brother,
and Jonadab was a wise man, etc."
Rav Yehuda says that Rav says:
A wise man for wickedness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of אמנון and תמר with another teaching of רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יונדב's wisdom was cleverness used for evil.

steps.title: יונדב's plan and the food תמר prepared
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוקים of יונדב's plan, then רב יהודה in the name of רב explains that תמר made fried foods for אמנון.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוקים say: 'Why are you so thin, son of the king... יונדב said to him: Lie on your bed and pretend to be sick,' up to 'and let her make the food in front of my eyes.' Then: 'She took the pan and poured it out before him.' רב יהודה said in the name of רב: She made him all kinds of fried foods.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the story by quoting יונדב's scheme. Then רב explains one detail: the food תמר made was fried food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says she took the מַשְׂרֵת (a pan) and poured out what was in it before him. רב explains that what she made for him was various kinds of fried food.

phrases.aramaic: ״וַיֹּאמֶר ... מַדּוּעַ אַתָּה כָּכָה דַּל בֶּן הַמֶּלֶךְ ...
phrases.english: "And he said... Why are you so lean, son of the king...
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 13:4–5. The dots mark words of the פסוק that the גמרא skips.

phrases.aramaic: וַיֹּאמֶר לוֹ יוֹנָדָב שְׁכַב עַל מִשְׁכָּבְךָ
phrases.english: And Yonadav said to him: Lie down on your bed
and pretend to be sick, etc."
until "and let her prepare the food before my eyes."
"And she took the pan and poured it out before him."
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 13:9.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
That she made him various kinds of fried foods.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: שֶׁעָשְׂתָה לוֹ מִינֵי טִיגּוּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of רב's comments on the אמנון and תמר story, right after calling יונדב wise for wickedness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'pouring' in the פסוק means תמר made him fried foods.

steps.title: Why did אמנון hate תמר so much?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק that אמנון hated תמר with a very great hatred, and asks why.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And אמנון hated her with a very great hatred.' What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about the story. It is setting up the next step, where רבי יצחק gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says his hatred was even stronger than his earlier love. That is strange, so the גמרא wants to know what caused such a sudden, extreme change.

phrases.english: "And Amnon hated her with a very great hatred."
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 13:15.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves forward in the story to a new detail and opens a question about it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The cause of אמנון's extreme hatred of תמר.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: a hair injured אמנון
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק answers that a hair became tied around אמנון and caused him a serious physical injury.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: A hair got tied around him and made him into a כרות שפכה (a man with a severed organ).
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק answers the question: אמנון was injured during the act, and that is why he hated her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hatred came from a physical injury he suffered. But the way it is worded ('a hair became tied') makes it sound like an accident, which the גמרא will question next.

keyTerms.meaning: A man whose organ has been severed (a halachic category of injury)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
A hair became tied around him
and made him into one whose organ is severed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: נִימָא נִקְשְׁרָה לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 38.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A hair became tied around אמנון and injured him, causing his hatred.

steps.title: If it was an accident, why blame her?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יצחק's wording: if the hair just got tied by itself, what did תמר do to deserve his hatred?
steps.simpleTranslation: But if the hair just got tied around him, what did she do?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. An accident is not her fault, so it does not explain why he hated her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is with the passive wording 'became tied'. If nobody did it on purpose, it is hard to see why אמנון would turn his anger against תמר.

keyTerms.meaning: But if / and is it so that

phrases.english: But if it became tied around him,
what did she do?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי נִקְשְׁרָה לוֹ, אִיהִי מַאי עֲבַדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of רבי יצחק's answer in step 39.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'נימא נקשרה לו' (a hair became tied).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An accident is not her doing, so it cannot explain why he hated her.

steps.title: Corrected wording: תמר tied the hair on purpose
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the wording: תמר herself tied a hair around him and caused the injury.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: She tied a hair around him and made him into a כרות שפכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of רבי יצחק's answer. תמר did it on purpose, so now his hatred makes sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only one word changes, from 'became tied' to 'she tied'. That turns an accident into her deliberate act, which explains why his hatred was aimed at her.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
She tied a hair around him
and made him into one whose organ is severed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 40 by changing the wording of step 39.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The hair got tied by accident.
steps.terutzMaskana: תמר tied the hair on purpose, which is why he hated her.

steps.title: רבא's teaching: Jewish women lack such hair
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer using רבא's teaching that Jewish women do not have hair in those places, so where would the hair have come from?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רבא taught: What is meant by the פסוק 'Your fame went out among the nations because of your beauty'? That Jewish women have no underarm hair and no hair in the private area!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the corrected answer. According to רבא, תמר as a Jewish woman should not have had such hair at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reads the 'beauty' of the Jewish people in the פסוק as a physical feature of Jewish women. If that is true, the story of a hair causing the injury seems impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: What is meant by what is written

phrases.english: Is that so?
But didn't Rava expound:
What is meant by what is written:
"And your fame went out among the nations because of your beauty"?
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 16:14.

phrases.english: That Jewish women do not have
neither underarm hair
nor hair in the private area!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the corrected answer of step 41 from an outside teaching.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that תמר used a hair to injure אמנון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא teaches that Jewish women do not have that hair, so the story could not have happened that way.

steps.title: תמר was different: daughter of a יפת תואר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that תמר was an exception, because her mother was a יפת תואר (a captive woman from another nation).
steps.simpleTranslation: תמר is different, because she was the daughter of a יפת תואר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge: רבא's teaching is about Jewish women in general, but תמר's mother was not born Jewish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses what רב taught earlier (step 34), that תמר was the daughter of a יפת תואר. So she is an exception to רבא's rule, and the hair explanation can stand.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman captured in war whom a soldier may marry under special Torah rules

phrases.english: Tamar is different,
since she was the daughter of a captive woman.
phrases.notes: This goes back to רב's teaching a few lines earlier that תמר was a יפת תואר's daughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי תָּמָר, דְּבַת יְפַת תּוֹאַר הֲוַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 42 by treating תמר as an exception.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: תמר, like all Jewish women, would not have had such hair.
steps.terutzMaskana: תמר's mother was a יפת תואר, so רבא's teaching does not apply to her.
steps.whatToRemember: The hatred is explained by a deliberate act of תמר. The challenge from רבא is answered because תמר was the daughter of a יפת תואר, which ties back to רב's earlier teaching.

steps.title: תמר's public mourning built a great fence
steps.stepSummary: On the פסוק of תמר putting ashes on her head and tearing her garment, a teaching in the name of רבי יהושע בן קרחה says she created a great protective fence, because people reasoned from her case to everyone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And תמר put ashes on her head and tore the striped robe she was wearing.' It was taught in the name of רבי יהושע בן קרחה: תמר built a great fence at that time. People said: If this can happen to princesses, all the more so to ordinary women. If this can happen to modest women, all the more so to women who are not careful.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next part of the story. A teaching says that because תמר cried out in public, everyone realized the danger and became more careful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her public mourning made the danger known to all. People used a קל וחומר: if even a modest princess was not safe, then surely ordinary and less careful women were at risk. That awareness acted as a 'fence' protecting others.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the name of
Women who are not careful about modesty

phrases.english: "And Tamar put ashes on her head
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 13:19.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶת כְּתֹנֶת הַפַּסִּים אֲשֶׁר עָלֶיהָ קָרָעָה״.
phrases.english: and tore the striped robe that was on her."

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה:
phrases.english: It was taught in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha:
Tamar built a great fence
at that time.
They said:
phrases.notes: He means the people who heard about what happened to her.

phrases.english: If this happens to daughters of kings,

phrases.aramaic: לִבְנוֹת הֶדְיוֹטוֹת עַל אַחַת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה.
phrases.english: to daughters of ordinary people, all the more so.
If this happens to modest women,
to women who are not careful, all the more so.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה: גָּדֵר גָּדוֹל גָּדְרָה תָּמָר בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next part of the story, after the discussion of the hatred is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תמר's public mourning made everyone aware of the danger, creating a protective fence for all women.

steps.title: רב: at that time a decree was made
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב begins to say that at that time the רבנן made a גזירה; the content continues in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: At that time they decreed…
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. רב starts to tell us about a גזירה made because of the תמר incident, and the details come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב connects the 'fence' just mentioned to an actual legal decree. The text stops here mid-sentence, so the content of the גזירה is not yet given.
steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is not finished here. Do not guess what the decree was; the גמרא tells us in the next lines.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
At that time they decreed

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה גָּזְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the 'fence' of step 44 by starting to describe an actual decree made then.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A decree was made at the time of the תמר incident (the content continues in the next section).
